# Reading notes: XQ published API contracts

Scope: all 140 pages in this snapshot. “Not found” means not found in these published pages, not proof that the server lacks the capability. These are documentation findings, not live conformance results.

| Question | Published answer | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| a. Webhooks | Manage `POST /hook` registers a hook to the API key. Body: required `url`, optional string-array `events`, `enabled` (default true), application `id` (defaults to request application). Dashboard API key and bearer; scope `hook`. Omitted/blank events subscribes to all events. `GET /eventtypes` lists workspace event identifiers and titles, including custom events. Twenty endpoint pages name webhook events (listed below). Callback payload contract, a complete static event catalogue, and confirmation of a normal key-fetch/read webhook are **not found**. Export events are explicitly documented but must not be equated with Validation FetchKey. `HookSummary` describes registration, not callback delivery. | [Create a hook](069fc5540d8c6-create-a-hook.md), [List event types](c543b524ef0bd-list-event-types.md), [EventType](074bb0931250e-event-type.md), [HookSummary](7108c0b0b040c-hook-summary.md) |
| b. Packet lifetime | `/packet`, single/multiple-key `/packet/add`: integer `expires` in hours in the structured schemas (some tutorials use a string). `/packet/batch`: per-entry integer `expires` plus string `unit`, default `days`; only `days` is illustrated, with no enum of supported units. Sub-hour units, fractional hours, an absolute-expiry input, a minimum and a never-expire value are **not found**. Retention article states a maximum of seven years and deletion on expiry. `dor=true` provides delete-on-read/one read per recipient. Packet summaries/details return `expires` as epoch milliseconds, which does not establish that creation accepts an absolute timestamp. `/expiration/{Locator}` reports seconds remaining. Separately, Send Email documents `expiration` in milliseconds; it does not document that as a key-packet creation option or specify absolute versus relative semantics. | [Create packet](a593767490467-create-a-new-key-packet.md), [Create/save](1f9bc1713a7cd-create-and-save-a-new-key-packet.md), [Batch](8e03fb4bd5ea0-create-and-save-multiple-key-packets-with-individual-metadata.md), [Batch entry](f3bbfd80618d1-key-packet-batch-entry.md), [Retention](922e0aadbd2e6-key-retention.md), [Expiry check](e5b0d6e2b5f5f-check-whether-a-key-is-expired.md), [Send Email](491a6ff428429-send-email.md) |
| c. META on events | Packet Summary/Details explicitly return `meta: string`, typically JSON serialized as a string. Event Summary/Details have `data: string`, possibly a serialized object with meta information; they do **not** promise that submitted packet `META` is echoed there. No event `meta` field or webhook payload contract is documented. Guaranteed packet-META propagation to events/log rows: **not found**. | [Packet Summary](8c7fe9a7159a3-key-packet-summary.md), [Packet Details](d16f78534e839-key-packet-details.md), [Event Summary](3dddf815a642f-event-summary.md), [Event Details](ca51c5a852842-event-details.md) |
| d. Fetch event row | Generic EventSummary fields: integers `id`, `app`, `key`, `val`, `threat`, `created`; strings `action`, `data`, `ip`, `location`, `user`, `appname`, `keyname`. Required: `id, action, app, key, val, threat, ip, created, appname, keyname`; data/location/user optional. EventDetails omits appname/keyname and adds `rev: boolean`, `others: string`; required `id, action, threat, ip, val, created, rev`. `key` is an API key ID, not the packet locator; `val` is a workspace user ID, or zero. `created` is documented in milliseconds, but epoch/zone is not explicit for this field. Audit Logs describes a `tz` query offset in hours from UTC, while the structured `/log` operation omits `tz`. A key-fetch-specific action name, mandatory locator/alias mapping, timestamp-zone guarantee, and sample fetch row are **not found**. The retention tutorial uses `/log?data=<locator>` to find associated logs. | [Event Summary](3dddf815a642f-event-summary.md), [Event Details](ca51c5a852842-event-details.md), [Search logs](6a56576f1cb4d-search-the-monitor-logs.md), [Audit Logs](83530d1aff0f1-audit-logs.md), [Retention](922e0aadbd2e6-key-retention.md) |
| e. Certificate management | Device authorization and optional device announcement are documented. Certificate issuance is described as happening in the management portal. API endpoints to create, list or revoke certificates: **not found**. Contact CRUD is documented, but is not described as certificate CRUD. | [Device authorization introduction](b2e549d6f9514-device-certificate-authorization.md), [Authorize certificate](eb5ecb08a475f-authorize-a-device-with-a-certificate.md), [Announce device](bb79491c661b9-announce-a-trusted-device.md), [Manage](a92720bfbb44a-manage.md) |
| f. Device token lifecycle | No refresh endpoint: obtain fresh `/time` then repeat certificate authorization with the same certificate. Certificates are long-lived and expected to outlive multiple tokens. Exact token TTL, certificate/key rotation protocol and effect of certificate revocation on already-issued tokens: **not found**. Authorization documents 403 for unknown/expired/revoked certificates; that establishes exchange refusal, not invalidation of existing bearer tokens. | [Device authorization introduction](b2e549d6f9514-device-certificate-authorization.md), [Authorize certificate](eb5ecb08a475f-authorize-a-device-with-a-certificate.md) |
| g. Token introspection | Manage `GET /session` checks a bearer token: 204 means valid; anything else means failure. No identity or rights response body. Separate `/subscriber` and Manage `/user` return user/contact information. An introspection endpoint that returns the token identity together with effective rights: **not found**. API-key validation is separate from access-token validation. | [Validate access token](f260b4a8eb1ea-validate-an-access-token.md), [Subscriber](0a40764acc475-get-information-about-the-current-user.md), [Current user](e0797f733fbe9-get-current-user.md), [Check API key](6d1bffdb02a92-check-if-valid-api-key.md) |
| h. Authorization policies | Govern access to encryption keys: authorized recipients, later recipient grants/revocation, location/country restrictions, groups, data types and labels. The Policy Manager example blocks a country mismatch and notifies the user. Retrieval also requires a valid unexpired user token, unexpired key and satisfied geofence. These are key-access controls; the documentation does not turn them into Opintel row/column policy or evidence of plaintext decryption. | [Key Authorization Policies](a6f5f085b4e4f-key-authorization-policies.md), [Retrieve key](2bc87668ba508-retrieve-a-key-with-its-token.md) |

## Boundaries and discrepancies worth retaining

- The certificate contract says full PEM text in `crt`. This snapshot does not revise that wording to match earlier probe findings; published contract and observed behavior remain distinct records.
- The batch schema includes the string `database`; the packet schemas still enumerate types 1–5 and do not establish numeric type 8. Do not treat the docs as a complete statement of account licensing or observed type-8 behavior.
- A page titled “Revoke Auth Token” describes revoking a message key, while its route is `/revoke`. This inconsistency is not evidence of certificate-revocation cascading to device tokens.
- EventDetails describes `others` as “No idea what this is for yet.” Its semantics remain unspecified.
- Publication statements about recipient-only access do not erase contrary historical probe observations. This pull makes no new recipient-binding claim.
